doc.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001

title: Listening to 'Elementals'
summary: Over an excerpt Brubeck says he wrote 'Elementals' in this house, built it as simple A-B-C sections, and explains why a skipped ninth sounds dissonant.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I had a little, a couple of excerpts here, that are separated by about 35 years I think. And maybe we can just listen to the tail end of this one.
You said you wrote that right in this room?
I finished it here. I started it in another house on the other side of town. Most of it was written right here.
You know this part right now sounds rather angry to me.
Oh? It’s really just [scats] A — B— C. Because I wanted it to be simple as A-B-C, and I wanted it in three sections. So the first section is in A, the second section in B and the last section in C.
That’s really interesting. Maybe it’s just the intervals that sound — plus everybody —
Well you know by spreading that interval it makes it, instead of one of the most used intervals, or like the A minor scale or something, all of a sudden it becomes dissonant by skipping up a ninth.
